q: A conflict arises between a House and a court over who determines the scope of privilege. Which statement is correct?
options: Privileges are subject to the Constitution, and the courts may determine their existence and extent
The House alone determines the existence and extent of its privileges conclusively
Privileges are outside the Constitution and are determined by the House alone
Privileges are determined by the President on a reference from the House
expl: Privileges operate subject to the Constitution and their existence and extent are examinable.
why: The historical dispute on this question is the reason the topic recurs in State papers.
trapnote: Privileges are constitutional in source and therefore examinable, whatever the House asserts.

q: Consider a Bill that would alter the representation of States in Parliament. Which statement is correct?
options: It needs a special majority alone, ratification being confined to Seventh Schedule changes
It needs a simple majority, being outside the amending procedure altogether
It needs a special majority and the prior concurrence of the affected States
It needs a special majority and ratification by not less than half the State legislatures
expl: Representation of States in Parliament is a federal provision requiring ratification.
why: The fourth option substitutes concurrence of affected States for ratification by half the legislatures.
trapnote: Ratification by half the States is required. Concurrence of affected States is a different thing.

q: An ordinary Bill is passed by the lower House and rejected by the upper House. Which statement is correct?
options: The Bill lapses and must be reintroduced afresh in the lower House
The President may summon a joint sitting, which decides by a special majority
The President may summon a joint sitting, which decides by a simple majority of those present
The lower House may pass it again after fourteen days and it is deemed passed
expl: A joint sitting decides by a simple majority of members present and voting.
why: The fourth option applies the Money Bill machinery to an ordinary Bill, which is the standard cross-wiring.
trapnote: The deemed-passage rule belongs to Money Bills. Ordinary deadlocks go to a joint sitting.

q: Consider the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council: 1-An Assembly resolution for its abolition was passed in 2020. 2-Parliament enacted the corresponding law. 3-The Council continues to function. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The resolution was passed and the Council continues because Parliament did not act.
why: The set is constructed so that the two true statements would ordinarily be inconsistent, which is the point.
trapnote: The resolution and the continuing Council coexist precisely because Parliament never legislated.

q: On the relative powers of a Legislative Council and the Assembly on a Money Bill, which statement is correct?
options: The Council may delay the Bill for fourteen days and may make recommendations only
The Council may reject the Bill, whereupon a joint sitting of the two Houses is summoned
The Council may amend the Bill, the Assembly being bound to consider the amendments
The Council has no role whatever in relation to a Money Bill of the State
expl: The Council mirrors the upper House at the Union level: delay and recommendation only.
why: The fourth option removes the Council entirely, which overstates a genuinely weak position.
trapnote: A Council is weaker than the Union upper House but not powerless. It may delay and recommend.

q: Consider: 1-The lower House alone may pass a resolution for the removal of the Vice-President. 2-The upper House alone may initiate such a resolution. 3-The resolution requires the agreement of the other House. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The upper House initiates and the lower House must agree.
why: The first statement reverses the initiating House, which is the natural assumption given where the Vice-President presides.
trapnote: Initiation lies with the House he presides over; agreement is required from the other.

q: A State legislature seeks to create a Legislative Council for itself. Which statement is correct?
options: The Assembly resolution requires a simple majority of members present and voting
The Assembly resolution requires ratification by half the State legislatures
The Assembly resolution requires a majority of total membership and two-thirds of those voting
The Assembly resolution requires the prior recommendation of the Governor
expl: The resolution requires a special majority of the Assembly.
why: The requirement is a special majority even though the resulting law of Parliament is passed like an ordinary law.
trapnote: A special majority for the resolution, an ordinary law for the enactment. The two differ.

q: Consider the Estimates Committee: 1-It has thirty members. 2-It is drawn from both Houses. 3-Ministers may not be elected to it. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Thirty members, all from the lower House, and ministers are excluded.
why: The single-House composition is the distinguishing feature of this committee among the financial committees.
trapnote: Estimates is the single-House committee. Accounts and undertakings draw from both.

q: A Bill is certified as a Money Bill and a member contends that it contains matters beyond the permitted list. Which statement is correct?
options: The certificate is declared final, though the extent of that finality is under reference
The contention is not maintainable in any forum, the certificate being conclusive for all purposes
The contention must be raised before the President, who decides the question
The contention is decided by the Chairman of the upper House on a reference
expl: Finality is declared by the text, and the extent of that finality is a live question.
why: The second option states the textual position as though no question could ever arise, which is the overstatement tested.
trapnote: The text declares finality; whether that ousts all review is the question under reference.

q: Parliament extends the term of the House during a Proclamation of Emergency. Which statement is correct?
options: The extension may be for two years at a time and ceases with the Proclamation
The extension may be for one year at a time and continues until fresh elections are held
The extension may be for the duration of the Proclamation without any annual limit
One year at a time, and not beyond six months after the Proclamation ceases to operate
expl: One year at a time, with a six-month tail after the Proclamation ends.
why: Each wrong option alters either the unit of extension or the tail period, so both variables must be held.
trapnote: Two variables: the annual unit and the six-month tail. Options vary one at a time.
